text: Wide World Importers rollout steering this morning w/ Stavros Dimitriou (COO, exec sponsor) and Clifford Abara (Head of IT, owns devices + network). Handheld scanner + WMS mobile rollout, 310 devices across 4 DCs: Dallas go-live Mon 16 Feb, then Memphis 9 Mar, Savannah 6 Apr, Reno 27 Apr. Our fee is $860k, billed per DC at each go-live. Stavros wants a go/no-go call the Thursday before each one.

Fourth Coffee renewal kickoff with Sunita Varghese (procurement mgr). Store Care contract (service desk + store network/POS support for 212 cafes) is $1.38M/yr and renews 17 Apr. We plan to go in at a 6% uplift - they added 40 cafes last year and our field tech wages are up. Sunita wants our proposal by Fri 13 Feb.
also from Sunita: their CFO Philippa Achterberg wants every commercial change shown as a redline against the current contract. No fresh proposal decks, she won't read them.

Trey Research: Dr. Shirin Farrokh (Head of Research IT) rang. January Azure bill came in at $61k vs their $48k monthly budget, a GPU cluster was left running 9 days after a protein-folding batch. Their CFO, Cornelius Ashdown, is asking questions. She needs our explanation by Wed.

draft a note to Shirin on the Azure overrun. The $13k is on us, our runbook had no auto-shutdown on the GPU pool. Fix: auto-stop after 4 hrs idle, budget alerts at 80% and 100%. Say we'll come back with a credit proposal by Thursday. Short, no excuses.

Fourth Coffee kiosk pilot planning w/ Reggie Mulcahy (VP Retail Ops) and Ezra Pemberton (IT Director). 12 Portland cafes, 2 self-order kiosks each, start Mon 9 Feb, runs 6 weeks. Success = avg ticket +8%, peak queue time -20%, kiosk uptime 99%. Our integration fee is $96k fixed. Ezra wants a PCI scan of the card readers before go-live.
Reggie: never book him 7-10am, that's the morning rush and he's out in stores. He'd rather do a quick Teams call than a long email thread.

WWI wifi survey results from Dallas: dead zones in the cold store, aisles 40-52. Jolanta Nowicka (Dallas DC ops manager) says handhelds drop out every few mins in the freezer section. We need 6 extra access points, change order $14,800 incl. install. Has to be in by 12 Feb or the 16 Feb go-live is at risk.

draft the change order cover email to Clifford: 6 extra APs for the Dallas cold store, $14,800 incl. install, need his approval by Fri so the kit ships in time to install by 12 Feb. Make clear the 16 Feb go-live depends on it.
Trey: agreed w/ my VP we'll credit half the overrun, $6,500, on the Feb invoice. Shirin is fine with that. Auto-stop and budget alerts went live today.

Kiosk readiness call w/ Ezra at 2pm. Prep me: what to check on PCI scope for the card readers, firmware versions, what happens to orders if a kiosk loses network, and the rollback plan if a cafe has problems on day one.

Fourth Coffee readiness: only 14 of 24 kiosks have arrived, the rest are due Tue. So pilot start slips from Mon 9 Feb to Wed 11 Feb. PCI scan booked for Mon 9 Feb. Ezra wants offline mode tested at 2 cafes before launch.

Trey: Shirin warned me Cornelius Ashdown never approves anything over $100k by email. He wants a 20-min call with the numbers on screen, Thursdays after 3pm only. The phase 2 SOW goes to him next week.

Trey contract facts so I stop digging: Research Cloud Ops (managed Azure + support) is $520k/yr and renews 15 May. Lab Data Platform phase 2 SOW is $410k - 14 instrument connectors, ELN integration, GxP validation pack. Kickoff targeted Mon 16 Feb.

draft a quick note to Reggie confirming the new kiosk pilot start, Wed 11 Feb, all 12 cafes. Remaining 10 kiosks land Tue and get installed overnight, PCI scan Mon. Offer a 10-min Teams call Tue afternoon if he wants a walkthrough.

WWI: Clifford approved the AP change order on the phone, PO to follow. Maeve Abernathy (procurement) confirmed the EDI migration RFP is out: responses due Fri 20 Feb noon, decision targeted 6 Mar. They're moving 62 trading partners off their old VAN.

Prep me for Thursday's 3:30 call with Cornelius Ashdown on the phase 2 SOW ($410k). He'll bring up the Azure overrun too. Give me the numbers in the order he'll want them, likely objections, and what I can concede.

Marguerite Castellano (WWI CFO) pushed back on the $14,800 AP change order. Her view: our original survey missed the cold store so we should eat half. Also fyi she wants every cost split by DC in an Excel attachment, never typed into the email body.
PCI scan on the kiosk card readers came back with 2 low findings (default SNMP string, an old TLS cipher on 3 units). Ezra's team is fixing tonight. Still go for Wed.
ugh, WWI: the AP vendor says the 6 access points won't arrive until 17 Feb. Dallas go-live slips from 16 Feb to Mon 23 Feb. Stavros grumbled but agreed, as long as Memphis stays 9 Mar.

draft a short update to Stavros and Jolanta: Dallas go-live now Mon 23 Feb because the APs land 17 Feb, install 17-18 Feb, coverage test Thu 19 Feb morning ahead of the go/no-go. Memphis still 9 Mar. Ask Jolanta to keep the training slots in the week of 16 Feb as dry runs.

Fourth Coffee kiosk pilot went live today in all 12 Portland cafes. By 10am: 410 kiosk orders. Hawthorne St cafe had a card reader freeze around 8:15, rebooted and fine by 8:40. Offline mode test passed at both test cafes yesterday. Reggie happy so far.

Prep me for the WWI EDI RFP response. Maeve's weighting: cost 40%, delivery approach 30%, references 20%, support 10%. We're planning $285k fixed for 62 trading partners. I hear Norvik Partners is bidding. What are our win themes and where are we weak?
what did we agree to credit Trey for the Jan Azure overrun again, and is it going on the Feb invoice?

Draft the Store Care renewal for Philippa Achterberg: 6% uplift on the $1.38M, plus a 3-yr option at 4.5% per year. Remember she wants it as a redline against the current contract, so give me a redline summary of the changed clauses (fees, term, kiosk support exclusion), not a proposal.

Cornelius call done. He wants the PO split: $150k before their FY ends 31 Mar, the rest from 1 Apr. Asked if the mass-spec connector can move to phase 3 to cut cost. Wants a revised SOW by Wed 18 Feb. Didn't mention the overrun once, good.

Trey: Mireille Dufresne (QA & validation lead) hasn't approved the validation plan. She wants a risk-based approach per GAMP 5 and needs ~3 more weeks. So phase 2 kickoff slips from 16 Feb to Mon 2 Mar. Shirin agreed, not thrilled.
Sent the Store Care renewal redline to Sunita at 11:30. 6% = $1,462,800 for 1 yr, or 4.5% per year on a 3-yr term. She'll put it in front of Philippa next week.

Jolanta (WWI Dallas): 120 pickers over 3 shifts need training, and she wants our trainers on the night shift too, 10pm-6am. Best time to reach her is 2pm right after shift change, never before 11am, she's on teh floor.

Draft the revised phase 2 SOW summary for Cornelius: mass-spec connector moved to phase 3, total down from $410k to $372k, PO 1 $150k by 31 Mar, PO 2 $222k from 1 Apr, kickoff Mon 2 Mar once Mireille signs off the validation plan. I'll walk him through it on screen Thursday.
remind me when Maeve's EDI RFP responses are due for WWI - is it this Friday at noon?

Philippa pushed back on the renewal, via Sunita: same-store sales down 3% in Q4, she wants it flat. Counter is 2% for 1 yr, or 3% per year on a 3-yr term, plus kiosk support folded into Store Care at no extra cost. My VP says our floor is 3.5%/yr on 3 yrs; kiosk support ok for the 12 pilot cafes only.

WWI: APs arrived today as promised. Install today and tomorrow, coverage test Thu morning before Stavros's go/no-go at 2pm. We accepted Marguerite's 50/50 split on the change order, so $7,400 each. Clifford is raising the PO for their half.

Draft the exec summary for our WWI EDI RFP response, addressed to Maeve Abernathy: $285k fixed, 14-week migration of 62 trading partners in 4 waves, 4-week parallel run, 30 days hypercare. Lead with low-risk cutover and our two distribution references. Keep it under 400 words.

Trey: Dr. Torben Aalund (Director of Lab Ops) complained instrument data takes ~6 hrs to show up in the platform, he wants under 1 hr. Phase 2 streaming ingestion fixes that. He wants plate readers done first, they're about 40% of his volume. Sent Cornelius the revised SOW summary this morning too.

Kiosk pilot week 1 numbers from Reggie (pilot started on Wed 11 Feb): kiosks took 27% of orders across the 12 cafes, avg ticket +11% on kiosk orders, peak queue time down 14% vs the -20% target. Card reader freezes at 2 cafes, Hawthorne St and Division St. Vendor firmware patch due Tue 24 Feb.

Stavros's Dallas go/no-go is at 2pm. Coverage test this morning: -67 dBm or better in every cold store aisle. Give me a tight go/no-go checklist (devices, network, training, badge/login sync, rollback) and the questions Stavros will ask.
Cornelius approved the $372k phase 2 in principle on today's call. PO 1 ($150k) to be raised by Fri 27 Feb. He also wants a monthly Azure spend summary from us, first week of every month.

Need to get back to Philippa's team next week on their counter. Lay out options between their 3%/3yr and our 3.5% floor - what can I trade instead of price? Thinking kiosk support for the pilot cafes, quarterly reviews, maybe a rate lock on the rollout (our list is $9,600 per cafe installed).

WWI handheld rollout went live at the Dallas DC this morning, all 86 devices on day shift, night shift picks them up tonight. Two pickers couldn't log in (badge sync), fixed by 10am. Fyi the EDI response went in Fri at 11:40, before the noon cutoff. Jolanta happy, Stavros walked the floor.
Trey news: Shirin Farrokh is promoted to Chief Data Officer from 1 Mar. Her deputy Jasper Thackeray becomes Head of Research IT and our day-to-day contact. Shirin stays exec sponsor for phase 2.
Fourth Coffee: Sunita is moving to their new franchise development team. Fergus Doyle takes over procurement and the Store Care renewal from 2 Mar. Sunita will intro us this week.

Big one at WWI: Clifford Abara is leaving, last day Fri 27 Feb. IT reports to Stavros for now. Jolanta Nowicka is promoted to Director of DC Operations and owns the remaining 3 rollouts. Still need a named IT contact for devices + network.
When does the Trey Research Cloud Ops contract renew again, and what's it worth per year?

ok, draft a short intro email to Jasper Thackeray as our new day-to-day: congrats, who's who on our side (Rhiannon Teague is delivery lead), phase 2 kickoff Mon 2 Mar, open items: PO 1 by Fri and Mireille's sign-off on the validation plan.

Draft the counter for Philippa Achterberg: 3.5% per year on a 3-year term, kiosk support included for the 12 pilot cafes, quarterly service reviews, and the kiosk rollout rate locked until 30 Apr. Same format as last time.

WWI Dallas, first 3 days since the rollout started on Mon 23 Feb: pick rate up from 92 to 104 lines/hr, mis-picks down ~30%. Night shift adoption slower, 6 pickers still on paper. Our trainers stay thru Fri.

draft a handover email to Clifford before he goes, cc Stavros and Jolanta. Open items: Memphis readiness for 9 Mar, their PO for the $7,400 AP half, the EDI decision on 6 Mar, and who owns network changes after Friday. Thank him properly, he's been good to us.

Trey: Mireille signed off the validation plan today. Her condition: all our validation docs in their template TR-QA-014, as Word with tracked changes, never PDF. Phase 2 kickoff Mon 2 Mar confirmed. PO 1 still not in.

Intro call with Fergus Doyle at 4. Give me a quick recap of where the Fourth Coffee renewal stands - what we proposed, Philippa's counter, what we sent yesterday - so I don't sound like I'm starting over with him.
Fergus Doyle (Fourth Coffee procurement, came over from their supply chain team) - sharp, numbers guy. He has our counter and wants a call with Philippa on Mon 2 Mar to close it out.

Maeve called: Wide World EDI shortlist is us and Norvik Partners. Norvik came in at $240k vs our $285k. She wants our best and final by Fri 6 Mar, decision moved from 6 Mar to Fri 13 Mar. Marguerite will sit on the final panel.

Trey PO 1 ($150k) landed Fri afternoon, just in time. Phase 2 kickoff done this morning, Jasper Thackeray chaired. Plate reader connector first per Torben, then HPLC and the 3 flow cytometers. Sprint 1 demo Thu 12 Mar. Rhiannon runs a weekly checkpoint with Jasper, Tuesdays 10am.

Fourth Coffee call w/ Fergus + Philippa. They'll take 3.5% per year on 3 yrs IF the kiosk rollout to 80 cafes is fixed at $8,900 per cafe installed (vs our $9,600 list), so $712k. Need to check install costs w/ delivery before I say yes. Promised an answer by Thu 5 Mar.

Prep the WWI best-and-final. Norvik is $240k, we're at $285k. Levers: cut the parallel run from 4 to 2 weeks, fixed-price cap, 30% of the fee at go-live. Marguerite Castellano will be on the panel - what will a CFO want to see, and what's the lowest number I can defend?
Delivery says $8,900 per cafe works if Fourth Coffee does the electrical prep themselves and we get 3 cafes per night per crew. Margin ~22%. OK to accept, but get the electrical prep in writing.
what were the success targets on the Fourth Coffee kiosk pilot again? want them in front of me for Thursday

Trey's Research Cloud Ops renews 15 May. Build me a renewal strategy summary: $520k/yr today, the Jan overrun and the $6,500 credit, the new budget alerts, how Cornelius likes to approve things, Jasper new in seat, Shirin now CDO. What uplift can we justify?

WWI Memphis: Jolanta wants to push go-live from 9 Mar to Mon 16 Mar, spring garden season inbound is peaking and she won't risk it. Stavros agreed. Memphis wifi survey was clean, no extra APs needed this time.

Pilot mid-point review with Reggie and Ezra tmrw 2pm. Prep me: week 1 vs latest numbers, the reader freezes and the 24 Feb firmware patch (none since), and what we need from them to make a rollout call once the pilot ends 25 Mar.
Trey: Jasper says Cornelius wants the Cloud Ops renewal proposal by Fri 20 Mar and is hoping for 0% uplift on a 2-year term. We'd pencilled 5%. Jasper reckons 2-3% on a 2-year would fly.

Kiosk mid-point review: kiosks now 34% of orders, avg ticket +12%, peak queue time -21%, uptime 99.4%. All targets hit. Reggie wants the go/no-go on the 80-cafe rollout Thu 26 Mar, the day after the pilot ends. Told Fergus we accept $8,900 per cafe as long as they do the electrical prep.

draft our WWI best-and-final cover letter to Maeve Abernathy: $262k fixed (down from $285k), parallel run cut to 2 weeks, 30% of the fee due at go-live, cap on change requests. Keep the letter to the commercial points, the cost breakdown by wave and DC goes in the Excel for Marguerite.
WWI best-and-final submitted at $262k, with the Excel cost breakdown by wave and by DC for Marguerite. Maeve confirmed reciept. Decision still Fri 13 Mar.
Trey Feb Azure bill: $46.2k, under the $48k budget. Alerts fired once at 80% on 24 Feb and their team shut an idle cluster within the hour. Nice story for the renewal.

draft the first monthly Azure spend summary Cornelius Ashdown asked for: Feb $46.2k vs $48k budget, Jan was $61k with the $6,500 credit applied on the Feb invoice, one alert fired and was handled. Keep it factual, no approvals in it.

Marguerite Castellano wants Wide World's app support contract ($310k/yr, renews 30 Jun) co-termed with their WMS licence on 31 May. So the current term ends a month early with June credited pro-rata, about $25.8k. She'd sign a 2-year renewal from 1 Jun if the rate holds.

Fergus: Philippa signed off the Store Care renewal at 3.5% per year for 3 years, kiosk support included for the 12 pilot cafes. Contract to us by Mon 16 Mar, signature target Fri 27 Mar, well before the 17 Apr renewal. Rollout price of $8,900/cafe held to 30 Apr.

Draft the Cloud Ops renewal proposal to Jasper, for Cornelius: 2-year option at 2.5% per year, or 1-year at 5%. Lead with the Feb bill under budget and the alerts working. Offer a quarterly cost-optimisation review. I'll take Cornelius through the numbers on a Thursday call, so the email just sets that up.

draft a thank-you + next steps email to Fergus Doyle: contract to us by 16 Mar, signature by 27 Mar, rollout rate $8,900 per cafe held until 30 Apr, electrical prep on their side confirmed in writing, go/no-go with Reggie Thu 26 Mar. Don't cc Philippa.

Draft my reply to Marguerite on the co-term: current app support ends 31 May instead of 30 Jun, June credited pro-rata ($25,833), new 2-year term from 1 Jun at the current $310k/yr. Numbers go in the Excel, not the email body.
Trey: Torben asked if we can add 2 more plate readers from their Basel lab to phase 2. Told him thats a change request and Jasper has to approve it. Rough estimate $18k.
Jolanta confirmed WWI Memphis go-live Mon 16 Mar: 74 devices, trainers booked incl. night shift. Stavros's go/no-go call is today at 2pm. Savannah 6 Apr still on.

Trey sprint 1 demo went well: plate reader data now lands in ~40 mins, down from ~6 hrs. Torben was grinning. Cornelius call at 3:30 too - he'll take the 2-year at 2.5% if the cost review is quarterly and in writing. Decision by Thu 19 Mar.
summarise where Trey Research stands for my 1:1 with my VP tomorrow: phase 2 status, PO 2 timing, Torben's Basel change request, renewal position. Short, he reads these on his phone.
Maeve just called - we WON the Wide World EDI migration at $262k! Contract by Fri 27 Mar, kickoff Mon 13 Apr. Norvik was cheaper but Marguerite liked the go-live milestone.
draft a thank-you to Maeve Abernathy and Marguerite Castellano for the EDI award. Confirm contract by 27 Mar and kickoff 13 Apr, and propose a planning workshop in the week of 30 Mar. Warm but short.

Fourth Coffee: Fergus sent the renewal contract early, today instead of Mon 16 Mar. One change from what we agreed: they want 45-day payment terms instead of 30. Need our finance team's view before I push back. Signature target still Fri 27 Mar.
